https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-antif.text: The EU’s antifraud watchdog said it has passed on to prosecutors allegations of potential corruption at the European Economic and Social Committee, a Brussels-based body that advises the EU on proposed legislation and policy. OLAF, the antifraud office, received a report from whistleblowers earlier this year saying there was a conflict of interest in the management of funds at the EESC, which is financed by the EU. It has now passed the case to the European Public Prosecutor’s Office. OLAF’s press office told POLITICO it had sent the case to EPPO but added that it could not comment further. Advertisement Advertisement The EPPO did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “The EESC was informed by OLAF yesterday that this case has been transmitted to the EPPO,” an EESC spokesperson told POLITICO. “Under these circumstances, the EESC cannot comment further except to re-confirm that when these matters first arose, the EESC president immediately and proactively referred the allegations to OLAF. The EESC will continue to respect fully the independence of this process.” Séamus Boland of Ireland was elected president in October 2025. “The EESC and its senior leadership take this matter very seriously and remain fully committed to integrity, transparency and accountability,” the spokesperson added. The EPPO has significantly stronger enforcement powers than OLAF. Whereas OLAF conducts administrative investigations, the EPPO investigates crimes against the financial interests of the EU, and can search private homes or seize evidence. OLAF has also been investigating a report that EESC executives tried to smoke out a staff whistleblower who raised the alarm about the funding concerns, the EU Ombudsman told POLITICO. Anonymous letters, seen by POLITICO, say that IT workers at the EESC were asked by senior managers to identify which staffers had connected to the OLAF website in previous weeks. The EESC said those anonymous letters contained “serious personal threats” and added that they were not made through the EESC’s “robust formal whistleblower process.” Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.insideindianabusiness.com/ar.text: The Dalton Foundry facility closed in May 2026. (Photo courtesy of Google Maps) Officials in Warsaw are hoping to bring a more than century-old foundry back to life after it closed earlier this year. Dalton Foundry LLC shut down operations after its former parent company, Michigan-based First Brands Group, filed for bankruptcy protection. But the company was acquired by MiddleGround Capital, a private equity firm headquartered in Lexington, Kentucky, which plans to invest $8.2 million in new equipment to restart the facility and bring back up to 125 jobs. The foundry produces iron castings used in a variety of industries, including automotive, agriculture, railroad, and air conditioning and refrigeration. The Warsaw Common Council last week approved a 10-year personal property tax abatement for the project. Jeremy Skinner, community and economic development director for the city, said the facility is currently not operational, which decreases its assessed value. "This company, MiddleGround Capital, is going to come in and put $8.2 million in new equipment, bring that property back into functional, bring the assessed value back to where it was or higher than what it was prior," Skinner said. "That increases the amount of property tax we receive off that project." While the facility itself is not operational, Warsaw Mayor Jeff Grose said the company currently employs 17 people with salaries totaling an estimated $1.2 million. He said the additional 125 jobs would bring that total to about $7.8 million. Dalton Foundry President Tony Goodman told the council that the company is in a position to take advantage of a shrinking foundry industry that has gone from 2,000 foundries in the 1980s to fewer than 200 today. Goodman said Dalton was the sole supplier of gray iron engine blocks in the United States, serving all of the major automotive manufacturers. He said he has been in contact with many of the company's past customers and has received "a lot of commitment" from them to come back as customers. He also noted that many of the previous employees who were laid off when the facility closed ready to come back to work. "They're stopping in weekly, letting us know that they're available to come back as soon as we can get a hold of them, or when we're ready to bring the people back," Goodman said. "I'm personally very excited. We get to rebirth and rebrand this location. I think the opportunity for Warsaw and Dalton Foundry to be as big as it once was in the 80s … we could be that again. There's no question." Goodman said if the tax abatement is approved and the financial investment is made, the foundry facility could be back up and running within 60 days. He credits that time frame to efforts to keep the facility from breaking down, which came with the help of some previous customers. "When we were officially closed, GM and Mercury Marine put an offer together to open us back up and run, and we did," he said. "So we built a lot of inventory for them. We built 10,000 engine blocks and about 24,000 heads in six weeks, produced them and finished them, and we kept the employees on to do that, and it was a major feat." When the facility closed earlier this year, about 262 employees were set to be laid off, according to a notice to the state. Goodman said there is potential in the future to add more workers beyond the 125 new jobs mentioned in the tax abatement request. Attorney Ross Benitz said MiddleGround Capital feels the foundry would fit well within its portfolio. "They are owner operators," Benitz said. "There is not a lot of interest in coming in, stripping it down, and taking the profits out. They are very interested and have a self-interest in the products that are produced at the foundry into the future. So they have a large incentive to see the foundry become successful." In addition to resuming production inside the facility, Goodman said he has plans to clean up the outside of the building, particularly in the rear that has been seen by some as an eyesore. He said his goal is to eventually put a mural on the outside of the building. A specific timeline for work to commence at the site and for hiring to begin was not provided.

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/mapa.text: Un incendiu care s-a declanşat duminică după-amiază într-un imobil de locuit din nord-estul Chinei s-a soldat cu cel puţin 14 morţi, a transmis luni agenţia publică de ştiri Xinhua . Incendiul s-a declanşat duminică, în jurul orei 17:00 (09:00 GMT) într-un imobil din oraşul Taiyuan, în provincia Shanxi, a precizat Xinhua în cursul serii. „În total, 38 de persoane au fost transportate la spital pentru a beneficia de îngrijiri medicale, dintre care cinci au murit”, a relatat agenţia, care ulterior a ridicat bilanţul la 15 morţi luni dimineaţă. Flăcările au fost stinse duminică şi operaţiunile de căutare şi salvare s-au terminat, a precizat Xinhua, citată de AFP și preluată de Agerpres. O anchetă este în curs pentru a stabili cauza incendiului. China a lansat o campanie împotriva riscurilor de incendiu în imobilele înalte în noiembrie 2025, după ce mai mulţi zgârie-nori au fost cuprinşi de flăcări la Hong-Kong, incident soldat cu 168 de morţi. O lună mai târziu, un incendiu într-un imobil rezidenţial din provincia Guangdong, în sudul Chinei, s-a soldat cu 12 morţi. În luna iulie, un incendiu într-o uzină de pantofi la Jinjiang, în provincia Fujian (sud-est), s-a soldat cu cel puţin 28 de morţi. Incendiile soldate cu morţi sunt relativ frecvente în ţară, din cauza normelor în construcţii laxe şi a unei abordări de multe ori neglijente în materie de securitate a muncii, comentează France Presse. Casa Albă a fost închisă temporar luni dimineață, după două incidente de securitate produse aproape simultan în apropierea reședinței președintelui american Donald Trump. Un bărbat a intrat cu mașina pe trotuar și a lovit un panou din Parcul Lafayette, în timp ce un altul a sărit peste o barieră de securitate, într-o zonă din apropiere. Amândoi au fost arestați, iar autoritățile consideră că incidentele nu au legătură între ele, relatează NBC Washington . Primul incident s-a produs în jurul orei locale 10:00 (17:00, ora României), când un autoturism argintiu a ajuns pe o alee pietonală din Parcul Lafayette, situat la nord de Casa Albă, și a lovit un panou cu informații istorice. Imaginile filmate de un jurnalist de la The Washington Sun arată mașina din care ieșea fum, înconjurată de agenți Secret Service și membri ai Gărzii Naționale. Șoferul a devenit agresiv în momentul intervenției forțelor de ordine, iar agenții au fost nevoiți să îl imobilizeze. „Șoferul a opus rezistență forțelor de ordine, dar a fost arestat rapid”, a transmis Secret Service într-un comunicat. Nu este clar de ce bărbatul a intrat cu mașina în zona pietonală. Ca măsură de precauție, echipa de geniști a poliției din Washington a verificat vehiculul pentru a se asigura că nu prezenta niciun pericol. În urma controlului, autoritățile au stabilit că mașina era sigură. Aproape în același timp, un alt bărbat a sărit peste un gard temporar de securitate, în apropierea intersecției dintre Pennsylvania Avenue și 17th Street, în colțul de nord-vest al Parcului Lafayette. „Aproximativ în același moment, o a doua persoană a sărit peste o barieră în apropierea colțului de nord-vest al Parcului Lafayette. Și aceasta a fost arestată rapid”, a precizat Secret Service. Bărbatul a fost ulterior transportat la spital, potrivit NBC Washington. Cele două incidente au determinat activarea măsurilor de securitate la Casa Albă. Jurnaliștilor aflați în complex li s-a cerut să rămână în sala de briefing din Aripa de Vest, iar accesul în zonă a fost restricționat. Măsurile au fost ridicate după aproximativ 30 de minute, iar activitatea a revenit la normal. Potrivit unei surse familiarizate cu ancheta, citată de NBC Washington, șoferul este acuzat de agresiune cu o armă periculoasă, acuzație legată de utilizarea vehiculului, precum și de agresarea unui polițist. Cel de-al doilea bărbat este acuzat de pătrundere ilegală. Motivele celor doi suspecți rămân necunoscute, iar ancheta este în desfășurare. Deși incidentele s-au produs aproape simultan și în aceeași zonă, autoritățile consideră că nu există o legătură între ele. Președintele Donald Trump se afla la Casa Albă în momentul incidentelor, potrivit Reuters. Urmărește știrile Digi24.ro și pe Google News
